correctness.rationale: The frozen result fixes a symmetric axial five-gon bipyramid with basal circumradius 1 and apex heights ±h (h>0); projection is orthographic with Haar normal and generic directions. Verified the reduction along u to the basal plane, whose hull is the pentagon plus two antipodal external points. Each visible edge chain of length k contributes g(0)=0 or g(k)=2−k; ordered edge-normal thresholds in 0<φ<π/10 have signs +,−,−,+,+ and yield precisely 5,6,7,6,5,4 as t increases. Integrating the thresholds G(c)=hc/sqrt(r²+h²c²) gives exact J_k=arcsin(λ sin(kπ/10))−arcsin(λ sin((k−1)π/10)), r=cos(π/5), λ=h/sqrt(h²+r²), and p4=(10/π)J5, p5=1−(10/π)(J1−J4+J5), p6=(10/π)(J1−J2+J3−J4), p7=(10/π)(J2−J3). All probabilities positive and sum 1. Derivative of p7 is 2gλ(b)−gλ(a)−gλ(c); the ratio of integrals of gλ'(x) on [b,c] and [a,b] strictly increases in λ, and endpoint signs oppose, establishing one global maximum, not merely a sampled optimum. Independently computed λ*=0.6712912804371369, h*=0.732718175591311 and max p7=0.08958840734036536. Independent true orthographic convex hulls for 5,000 Gaussian/isotropic directions at each of h=.1,h*,1,3 matched the 4-class law to sampling error. These finite checks corroborate the uniform-in-h calculus proof, not replace it.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the exact four-atom Haar random orthographic shadow law uniformly for h>0 and unique optimizing seven-vertex height. McGuire's silhouette theorem and Black–Criado's random-shadow theorems control expectations/bounds of general polytopes, not the specific full law and optimizer; Glisse–Lazard gives general average upper bounds. Closest Resultary laws for rectangular pyramids and stretched octahedra concern different geometries. The five-edge ordering and monotone derivative comparison supply genuine additional mathematics.
residual_risks: General computational geometry literature could contain a hidden equivalent law under shadow-chamber/normal-fan terminology, and its full historical bibliography has not been exhaustively read.
A finite numerical optimum without the monotone analytic argument would not establish uniqueness; here the analytic argument is part of the audited proof.

value.rationale: The pentagonal bipyramid is a natural seven-vertex test object with an actual geometrically distinguished Johnson height. Its 4/5/6/7-vertex Haar shadow law over a continuous shape parameter and a unique height optimizing the rare full-seven-vertex visibility event are substantive exact integral-geometric invariants. The Johnson shape is demonstrably suboptimal; the result can benchmark visibility and silhouette optimization without requiring a universal theorem for all polyhedra.

limitations: Only symmetric axial pentagonal bipyramids and Haar orthogonal projection; nongeneric directions measure zero.
General silhouette bounds and analogous different-polytope optimizers are known; unindexed exact pentagonal law remains a priority risk.
